english.title: Make / recklessly make a false statement to licensing authority - Activity Centres
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) for the purpose of obtaining or holding a licence under the Adventure Activities Licensing Regulations 2004 made a statement knowing that it was false, or recklessly made a statement which was false, in a material particular namely **(..SPECIFY THE FALSE STATEMENT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 16 of the Adventure Activities Licensing Regulations 2004 and section 2(1)(b) and (2) of the Activity Centres (Young Persons' Safety) Act 1995.
english.pointstoprove:
date and place
for the purpose of obtaining or holding a licence
made a statement knowing that it was false OR
recklessly made a statement which was false in a material particular

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence applies to the Adventure Activities Licensing Regulations 2004, regulation 16

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
